title: Thrust
build: TCI crack of the Firebird release, one packed file on a D64; level 1 in play

credits.role: original game, on the BBC Micro (Wikipedia, C64-Wiki)

accuracy.note: Bronze run: 25 routines and tables named after the sweeps
Silver run: the whole program described, from 15.7 % to 100 %

exclude: The crack's BASIC line (SYS 2082) and the start of its first depacker, left from loading. The game never reads them: no instruction or pointer names an address here.
Bytes left from loading between the direction tables and the messages. No instruction or pointer names them.
Two bytes after the messages copied to $0900, left from loading. Nothing reads them.
Bytes left from loading after the direction tables. scroll_and_window's base $09F7 is only used with X from 9, which starts at $0A00.
Bytes left from loading after the column tables. $0BFF is only a base address that swap_sprite_lists uses with X from 1.

Data left from the crack's loading and unpacking: the same at the hand-over as in play, and never read. No instruction names an address here, no pointer the game sets reaches it, and the video chip looks only at $4000-$7FFF. It decodes as neither code nor text (packed data, by its look).

The rest of the relocator's source: the crack's relocator copied $3000-$6CFF up to $8280 and left this behind, a stale copy of $8281-$927F (4,061 of 4,095 bytes still equal in play; the rest differ where the game changes its own variables). Only $3000 is used, by raster_handler_0's JSR $3000.

Data left from loading, the same at the hand-over as in play, that nothing reads: no instruction or pointer names it, and no sprite pointer the game writes ($00-$30, $4C-$4F) reaches it. It shows as noise if drawn as sprites.

Video memory the game writes as it runs: the rod's two sprite buffers ($5300-$53FF, drawn by draw_rod), the second colour screen and its sprite pointers ($5400-$57FF), the status bar's character set ($5800-$5AFF, a copy of status_bar_chars that print_char writes figures into; $5B00-$5BFF after it holds bytes left from loading that no character shown uses), and the main colour screen and its sprite pointers ($5C00-$5FFF, filled by set_level_colours and text_page).
The bitmap: the status bar's copy at $6000-$627F (hidden under the text-mode status bar) and the play area, drawn and cleared as the game runs.
Bytes below the relocated program, left from loading and never read.

Left from loading above the program: the crack's relocator itself ($BE96-$BEC6, carried up from $6C16 with the program it moved), the first $B9 bytes of the sprite data it had copied to $4000 ($BEC7-$BF7F), and from $BF80 bytes the relocator never wrote. Nothing runs or reads them.

TCI's loading picture, unpacked into the RAM under the I/O before the game starts: the code at $D000 that shows it and the colours it copies from $D800-$DBFF into colour RAM (orientation.md, step 2). The game keeps the I/O in.

Under the KERNAL, which the game keeps in: TCI's loading picture's bitmap ($E000-$FF3F, shown from video bank 3 by the code at $D000 before the game starts) and the bytes after it. The game never reads them.
